t: I know which floorboard complains when I step on it. I should fix that.
The room still smells like fresh timber when the door has been shut all day.
I need another peg by {the door|my bed}. One peg is never enough.
I left mud across my own floor again. At least it is my mud and my floor.
The fire draws better since I moved that stone. Small changes matter in a house.
I should air the {blankets|bedding} tomorrow. They have started smelling like smoke.
There is a draft under the door, but I know where to stuff the cloth now.
I keep a cup by {the bed|my chair}. It makes the place feel settled.
The roof creaks in the wind, and every time I count the beams again.
I could use a shelf near {the hearth|the door}. Everything ends up on the floor.
I swept yesterday, and somehow there are leaves inside again.
A shut door at night is worth more than I knew.
We disagree about where everything belongs. Somehow it all stays where they put it.
They steal the blanket every night and deny it every morning.
I should get home early tonight. We have barely spoken all {week|day}.
The house feels different when they are not in it. Too quiet by half.
We need a bigger pot. Marriage has somehow doubled the washing up.
They fixed the latch without saying anything. I noticed.
We keep planning a quiet supper. Something always needs doing first.
I still look for them in a crowd before I realize I am doing it.
I should apologize before night. I was tired, but I was still wrong.
They worry too much when I work late. I suppose that is better than not worrying.
I promised we would eat together tonight. I mean to keep it.
The best part of coming home is having somebody notice.
I need to mend the net before that tear becomes the whole net.
The fish were biting close to shore. That saved me a long wet walk.
I lost a good {hook|weight} today. I am more annoyed than it was worth.
The water looked empty all morning, then the net came up heavy.
Cold fingers make poor knots. I need better gloves.
I know there are fish under me. Knowing does not fill the basket.
I found {berries|another patch} where I was certain we had picked everything clean.
The basket is heavier on the way home. That is the satisfying part.
I keep seeing good patches after my basket is already full.
Half this work is remembering what will be ripe next week.
I ate one berry to check it. Then I checked another.
The birds always find the good bushes before I do.
That tree leaned the wrong way all morning and fell exactly where I expected.
I need to wrap this axe handle before it {opens|blisters} my palm again.
The close trees are gone. Every log now starts with a long walk.
I planted saplings today. Somebody else will be glad I did.
Fresh chips stick to everything. I will be finding them in bed.
A dull axe turns one job into three. I know better than this.
The tracks doubled back at the creek. I nearly missed it.
I waited so long today that my feet went numb before anything moved.
The {spearhead|binding} is loose again. I should fix it before I trust it.
I saw plenty of signs and no meat. Signs do not make stew.
A clean trail is easy. It is the broken trail that teaches you anything.
I came back empty, but I know where to start tomorrow.
People want certainty from a priest. I mostly have questions and a clean robe.
I should visit the family with the new baby. They will need food more than advice.
The shrine needs sweeping again. Dust does not care where it settles.
I heard three prayers today and had an answer for none of them.
A short sermon would do everyone good, especially me.
I need to listen longer before I tell people what their trouble means.
